items.headline: Comey hit with new Espionage Act charges
items.summary: The Justice Department filed additional charges against former FBI Director James Comey over alleged leaks to the media. It is the third criminal case brought against Comey.

items.headline: Israelis vote in election seen as referendum on Netanyahu
items.summary: Israelis went to the polls Tuesday in a Knesset election pitting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc against an opposition led by former general Gadi Eisenkot. The Nation examined what a change in government could mean for Palestinians.

items.headline: Anthropic files for a potentially record-setting IPO
items.summary: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, filed for an initial public offering that could be among the largest ever. The AI company has not yet set a share count or price range.

items.headline: Brazil widens money laundering probe of Flávio Bolsonaro
items.summary: Brazilian authorities are expanding a money laundering investigation involving Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's runoff to President Lula. Bolsonaro has refused to concede and asked for the result to be annulled.

items.headline: House Democrats' Epstein report details 1993 allegation against Trump
items.summary: A staff report from House Judiciary Committee Democrats on President Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein includes new details of a 1993 rape allegation against Trump. The report was released a week before the midterm elections.

items.headline: China's Communist Party opens key plenum
items.summary: A closed-door plenum of the Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee began Monday, with Xi Jinping seeking stronger party discipline. The meeting comes about a year before Xi is expected to seek a fourth term.

items.headline: Poll watchers from both sides prepare for Election Day
items.summary: Thousands of observers from the right and left are expected at polling places on Nov. 3. Democratic and nonprofit groups are training volunteers to report activity they find concerning.

items.headline: Trump steps up anti-Muslim attacks on Michigan's El-Sayed
items.summary: President Trump called Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a security threat and questioned his loyalty. Barack Obama campaigned with El-Sayed in Michigan and sharply criticized Trump.

items.headline: GOP-drawn districts turn into costly battlegrounds
items.summary: Republicans who redrew congressional maps to favor their party are spending millions to defend several of those districts. Some of the seats remain competitive heading into the midterms.

items.headline: Two in three new cars sold in China were electric
items.summary: Plug-in hybrids and fully electric vehicles made up two of every three new passenger cars sold in China in September, according to industry data. Yale Environment 360 reported the figures on Monday.

digest.overview:
The Justice Department unsealed two Espionage Act counts against former FBI Director James Comey over a 2016 leak, which he denies. A federal appeals court dismissed the department's emergency bid to set aside about 20,000 California mail ballots tied to suspected noncitizens. Democrat Mary Peltola asked a judge to toss the administration's suit seeking to block Alaska's Senate certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan narrowly loses. President Trump rallied in Mississippi and offered $1 million for tips leading to election-fraud convictions. House Judiciary Democrats released an Epstein report with new details of a 1993 allegation against Trump. Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq, reporting $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, and Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees.

Abroad, Israelis voted in a Knesset election with the highest morning turnout since 1981, after final polls showed neither Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's reaching a 61-seat majority. Russia struck Kyiv overnight with 16 ballistic missiles and 280 drones, killing one person, as a U.S.-brokered local ceasefire for aid took effect in occupied Oleshky. A U.N. inquiry said Israel committed crimes against humanity in the West Bank, which Israel rejected. Brazil widened a money laundering probe of Flávio Bolsonaro, who is still contesting Lula's win. China's Communist Party opened a four-day plenum seen as setting up a fourth term for Xi Jinping. South Korea's ruling Democratic Party will seek a parliamentary probe of Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, and Kim Jong Un pledged deeper North Korean ties with Vietnam. Bulgaria's presidential race heads to a Nov. 1 runoff.

home.overview:
Milwaukee is one win from its first World Series title after routing Tampa Bay 10–1 in Game 3, scoring eight two-out runs in the fifth as Robert Gasser threw six shutout innings and Jackson Chourio collected four hits; Game 4 is tonight at Tropicana Field. Dallas beat Philadelphia 38–21 on Monday night, dropping the Hurts-less Eagles to 2–5 with a fifth straight loss, and Week 8 kicks off Thursday with Panthers at Packers as the trade deadline chatter grows. In the NBA, Golden State hammered Denver 134–114, Boston crushed Chicago 134–99 and Cleveland outlasted Minnesota 127–125 in overtime; Pistons at Knicks and Blazers at Lakers headline tonight.

PSG beat Lyon 2–0 with two late goals to go top of Ligue 1, and Sevilla's 2–0 win over Osasuna closed La Liga's weekend with Barcelona two points clear of Atlético after Mbappé's 100th Madrid goal decided El Clásico. The Carabao Cup fourth round starts tonight with Fleetwood hosting Arsenal before Liverpool–Chelsea on Wednesday, and Saturday brings Der Klassiker in Munich. In the KBO, Kia took Game 1 of its second-round series 5–1 at Samsung, with Game 2 tonight in Daegu.

brief: Kia beat Samsung 5–1 in Game 1 of the best-of-five second round Monday in Daegu.
Harold Castro and Han Jun-su homered, and Kim Do-yeong starred as Samsung managed only two hits.
Kia's manager credited his bullpen for the road win.
Game 2 is Tuesday at 6:30 p.m. KST in Daegu, with Ariel Jurado starting for Samsung and Adam Oller for Kia.
The series moves to Gwangju for Games 3 and 4, and the winner meets KT Wiz in the Korean Series.
